- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply a 1–3 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 1–3% after spike.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model shows mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of recent history.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term downward trend; apply a 10–15% downward bias if sentiment is negative or if recent 10-day average is falling.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.5), model overfits short-term momentum; reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 7–14 days.
